catalog_quote: p.15: "4. ACCENT In order to obtain a good pronunciation of these languages, especially of Ndogo, great attention must be paid to the accent. The following suggestions (I shall not call them rules) may serve as a guide for Ndogo. ... III. The most noteworthy difference in accent exists among words of two syllables, some having an even stress on both syllables, and some having a real accent on the first. ... V. Bviri. Most of the remarks made for Ndogo hold good. Moreover note the following: (a) the final vowel of such words as those spoken of in III., especially if that be « i » and the consonant be « n », is often dropped" p.29: "accent usually lies on the first syllable of dissyllables"

sources.locator: p. 75, sec. 1 'Le système vocalique du viri'
sources.note: Acoustic/perceptual study of the 7-vowel system (i ɪ ɛ a ɔ ʊ u; formants F1-F3, one speaker, perception test). Tone is mentioned only in passing and first-hand: the seven example words in Fig. 1 all carry a mid tone, marked with a macron over the vowel, so that the vowels contrast in an identical (tonal) context. No tone inventory, no tone section beyond this sentence; the existence of a 'ton moyen' implies a multi-level register system consistent with the H/M/L of the a work listed here.
